back: N replicas per key; a write succeeds after W acks; a read waits for R responses and returns the newest version.

front: Failures tolerated by N, R, W?
back: Writes survive N − W dead replicas; reads survive N − R.
The R-th fastest replica's response time (writes: the W-th fastest ack).

front: Three 99% replicas: P(2 of 3 up) vs P(3 of 3 up)?
back: 0.999702 vs 0.970299. Requiring all replicas is worse than one node.

front: Cassandra QUORUM with two DCs at RF 3?
back: ⌊6 ÷ 2⌋ + 1 = 4 replicas, so it crosses the WAN. LOCAL_QUORUM needs 2 in the local DC.

front: Why does R + W > N guarantee overlap?
back: Pigeonhole: disjoint read and write sets would need W + R distinct replicas, more than N exist.
Makes any two write quorums overlap, so two conflicting writes can't both succeed on disjoint replicas.

front: Does R + W > N give linearizability?
back: No. Concurrent writes, partially failed writes, restores from stale copies and sloppy quorums all break it.

front: A QUORUM write fails. Was the data written?
back: Possibly, on the replicas that acked. It can later become visible, so retries must be idempotent.
When home replicas are unreachable, writes go to the next healthy nodes on the preference list and count toward W.
A stand-in stores the write with a hint naming its home replica and forwards it when that replica returns.

front: Do Cassandra hints count toward consistency level?
back: No, except for ANY. Hints are kept only for nodes down less than max_hint_window (3 hours by default).
On a read, the coordinator writes the newest version back to replicas that returned older ones.
Data nobody reads is never repaired; that needs anti-entropy.
Leaves hash key ranges, parents hash children. Compare roots, descend only where hashes differ.

front: Why must Cassandra repair run within gc_grace_seconds?
back: Otherwise tombstones are purged before every replica has them, and a stale replica resurrects deleted rows.
